description: Exact RGBs in M4's final 16-color quantized palette eligible for palette-variant remapping. Only the shirt (top) and trousers families are listed — skin, hair, and the beard (a hair-family feature) are never remapped, matching the roster-integration structural decision (#2).

top.note: Dominant bone-grey shirt fill (verified via strap-clear sample rectangles on front chest + back).
Shoulder highlight tone; appears only on back.png (rows 19-22), clean, no cross-role sharing found anywhere in the file.

trousers.note: Second fold-shading tone; distinct pixel cluster from trousers-shade, both verified clean.

excludedFromRemap.note: The roster plan's named risk for M4 — grey hair vs. bone-grey shirt being close in tone — was checked with full-file pixel scans (not just sample rectangles), per ROSTER_PIPELINE_NOTES.md's guidance that the ASCII legend alone can mislead. Verdict: hair and shirt occupy fully separate silhouette regions (hair rows 0-18, shirt rows 19+) and never spatially merge or bleed into each other anywhere in front/back/side — confirmed both numerically (the hair family (128,116,104)/(172,152,129)/(92,83,67) and shirt family (218,192,150)/(222,198,156) are distinct clusters) and visually (zoomed crops of the beard, the hairline-to-collar boundary on the back view, and the crown). An EXACT-VALUE sharing was previously found here (shirt-main (218,192,150) doubling as a handful of hair-crown highlight pixels, 6-10px per reference view at the very top of the head) — RESOLVED (R3 review fix) by `character-pipeline/retint_m4_hair.py`, which retints every hair-crown occurrence (y<=12 across all 8 packed source files, verified via a full before/after pixel diff to touch zero shirt pixels, y>=17) to a new dedicated (217,193,152) hair-highlight tone that is not a member of any remap table's 'from' list, so it is immune to garment-variant remapping regardless of which palette a given being resolves to. shirt-main (218,192,150) itself is now used ONLY for the actual shirt fill.

suggestedVariant.name: violet-grey
suggestedVariant.note: One example remap into the world's muted garment families (BEING_PALETTE_VARIANTS in beingPalette.ts: slate-blue / violet-grey / moss / ochre / bone). M4 already ships in a bone-adjacent tone, so 'violet-grey' is proposed instead for visually distinct variant testing — re-validate visually against the actual atlas render before locking in for R3.
